film.title: Lucky Seven: The Seventh Governors of the Ivy League States
film.description:
Count the governors of the seven Ivy League states from independence and stop at number seven. You get seven men almost nobody remembers: Roger Griswold of Connecticut, James Fenner of Rhode Island, Joseph C. Yates of New York, James Sullivan of Massachusetts, William Plumer of New Hampshire, Mahlon Dickerson of New Jersey and George Wolf of Pennsylvania. Seven chapters, seven facts each, and one question running through all of them: who got a say, and who got left out?

Chapters
Connecticut: Roger Griswold, Yale class of 1780
Rhode Island: James Fenner, Brown class of 1789
New York: Joseph C. Yates (Columbia and Cornell's state)
Massachusetts: James Sullivan (Harvard's state)
New Hampshire: William Plumer (Dartmouth's state)
New Jersey: Mahlon Dickerson, Princeton class of 1789
Pennsylvania: George Wolf (Penn's state)

Narrated by Matthew Hagan, in his own voice cloned with AI. Gary Mercer, Thurston Whitmore, Barnaby Thayer, Henrietta Morningside, Libby Hartwell, Prudence Ashworth, Winnie Hollis, Chip Van Doren and Benjamin Quill are fictional AI anchors with AI voices. Governors are numbered from independence, the way each state's standard list counts them; some states count differently, and the film says where.

Pictures from Wikimedia Commons, each credited on screen with its author and license. Music is original, including an arrangement of "Yankee Doodle" (public domain).

Local history... and college basketball. See more at https://hardwoodbricks.com

reels.title: Roger Griswold, Connecticut's 7th governor, and the cane on the House floor
reels.text: In 1798 a Yale man named Roger Griswold took a cane to a congressman on the floor of the House. In 1811 Connecticut made him governor. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.

reels.title: James Fenner, Rhode Island's 7th, 11th and 17th governor
reels.text: James Fenner was governor of Rhode Island three times, so he is the state's 7th, 11th and 17th. His last stint began right after the Dorr Rebellion, the 1842 fight over who got to vote. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.

reels.title: Joseph C. Yates, New York's 7th governor, and the vote in 1821
reels.text: Joseph C. Yates of Schenectady was the first governor elected under New York's 1821 constitution, which opened the polls to working white men and shut out nearly all Black men. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.

reels.title: James Sullivan, Massachusetts' 7th governor, taught himself the law
reels.text: No college. Self-taught at home after a childhood injury. James Sullivan became Massachusetts' 7th governor in Harvard's backyard. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.
